# TryRaisins

> TryRaisins is a software engineer whose work is used by FTSE 100 companies on four continents, building web products, developer tools and open-source projects, mostly with Next.js, Node.js and Python.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/
Source revision: f9d54a7

## Projects

- [Terror Tracker](https://terrortracker.tryraisins.dev/) (2026, Live incident map): A map for exploring verified security incidents and emerging patterns across Nigeria.
- [SlopLens](https://sloplens.tryraisins.dev/) (2026, Design audit tool): Scores any web page out of 100 for how template-made it looks, and lists the tells that gave it away.
- [QuickBillz](https://quickbillz.tryraisins.dev/) (2026, Invoicing product): A straightforward way to create and share invoices, without a monthly subscription.
- [Talent Hunter](https://talenthunter.tryraisins.dev/) (2026, Resume matching): Compares resumes with a job brief to help teams build a clearer shortlist.
- [StreamSlip](https://streamslip.vercel.app/) (2025, Music utility): Turns YouTube Music listening history into a tidy recap you can share.
- [yeknal](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/) (2026, Developer tooling): A command-line tool and a library of agent skills that teach coding agents how I review, design, test and ship work.
- [BetPicks](https://betpicks.tryraisins.dev/) (2026, Sports picks product, currently unavailable): A single place to look through fixtures, odds, and match predictions.

## Agent skills

The library has 57 agent skills, and every one has a page and a markdown version at the same path with a `.md` suffix.

- [Agent skills library](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/): every skill, grouped by the task it serves.
- [Library as markdown](https://tryraisins.dev/skills.md): the same list in one fetch.
- [Skills source on GitHub](https://github.com/tryraisins/MD_Files): the files each skill installs.
- [yeknal on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/yeknal): the command-line tool that installs the same skills.

# Agent skills

> 57 free agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other coding agents, grouped by the task each one serves.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/
Source revision: f9d54a7

## How to install

Each skill page carries an install prompt pinned to a published revision, with a file list and SHA-256 hashes so an agent can verify what it fetched.

## Plan and build

- [Implement](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/implement.md): Takes a scoped feature or fix from plan to working code while keeping the rest of the repository behaving as it did.
- [App performance](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/performance.md): Measures startup, screen navigation, content loading and scrolling on a throttled production build, finds the real bottleneck, then proves each fix with before and after benchmarks rather than intuition.
- [Code graph](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/code-graph.md): Builds a local, model-free index of a repository and answers with a small ranked slice, so an unfamiliar codebase can be entered in one call instead of many searches.
- [Design system](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/design-system.md): Builds, audits, documents or migrates a product's design system: token layers, mapping hardcoded values onto tokens, component specs, drift detection and an ordered adoption plan.
- [Domain modeling](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/domain-modeling.md): Clarifies a project’s domain terms and boundaries and records the decisions in a glossary or architecture decision record.
- [Frontend developer](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/frontend-developer.md): Implements or repairs accessible web interfaces in React, Vue or Angular, covering components, state, styling and browser behaviour.
- [Legacy sweep](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/legacy-sweep.md): Audits a whole repository or subsystem for unused legacy code and bloated or worthless tests, proves each candidate is obsolete before deleting it, fixes real defects instead of removing the failing test, and keeps the coverage that still protects behaviour.
- [Mobile app design](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/mobile-app-design.md): Designs and builds mobile screens and flows that feel native, especially in Expo or React Native, covering navigation, controls, states, accessibility and performance.
- [Orchestration specialists](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/orchestration-specialists.md): Organises work across several agents and tools, covering task distribution, context management, evidence synthesis, prompt engineering and MCP design.
- [Pick a UI library](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/pick-ui-library.md): Recommends the right library or inspectable source registry for a frontend need from a curated list, from accessible primitives to charts, toasts and drag and drop.
- [Raise the bar on a brief](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/ambition.md): Raises a task or prompt to expert standard before work starts, by finding the real bottleneck and naming the raw material, the method and the outside check that decides whether the result is right.
- [Research and analysis](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/research-analysis.md): Researches and compares sources, checks them against each other and writes evidence-backed reports for market, competitive, trend or data questions.
- [Verification harness](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/verification-harness.md): Generates a project-local skill that launches the real app, drives a feature the way a user would, and captures proof, with a feature map for the next agent to follow.

## Design interfaces

- [Frontend design](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/frontend-design.md): Sets a distinctive visual direction for new or heavily reshaped UI, from typography and composition to palette and interface copy.
- [Redesign an existing product](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/redesign-existing-projects.md): Refreshes the look or flow of a working site or app without breaking its behaviour or the data behind it.
- [Apple-style interface design](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/apple-design.md): Brings Apple’s approach to fluid, physical motion and interface design to the web, from springs and interruptible gestures to materials, depth and typography.
- [Brand kit images](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/brandkit.md): Generates polished brand-guideline boards, logo systems and identity presentations as images, with deliberate composition and sparse typography.
- [Break UI](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/break-ui.md): Stress-tests a screen with realistic worst-case data, such as long names, missing fields, huge counts and non-Latin text, and reports every break with its fix.
- [Content and SEO](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/content-seo.md): Guides useful content and search visibility together, from keyword patterns and page briefs to metadata, structured data, sitemaps, local search, earned links and AI citations.
- [Design reference research](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/design-reference-research.md): Researches comparable products and collects references into an evidence ledger and brief, so design decisions come from what works rather than what’s fashionable.
- [Design system](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/design-system.md): Builds, audits, documents or migrates a product's design system: token layers, mapping hardcoded values onto tokens, component specs, drift detection and an ordered adoption plan.
- [Design taste for the web](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/design-taste-frontend.md): Designs and builds expressive landing pages, portfolios and marketing sites from real product evidence instead of reusable AI layouts.
- [Frontend developer](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/frontend-developer.md): Implements or repairs accessible web interfaces in React, Vue or Angular, covering components, state, styling and browser behaviour.
- [High-end visual design](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/high-end-visual-design.md): Creates art-directed, showcase-level web interfaces with a product-specific visual idea, expressive type, deliberate composition and considered motion.
- [Human-AI interface design](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/human-ai-interface-design.md): Designs AI features people can trust, covering suggestions, generation, copilots and agents, along with sources, uncertainty, approvals and recovery.
- [Industrial brutalist UI](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/industrial-brutalist-ui.md): Designs raw, mechanical interfaces that mix Swiss print typography with terminal aesthetics: rigid grids, extreme type contrast and utilitarian colour.
- [Minimalist UI](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/minimalist-ui.md): Designs clean editorial interfaces with warm monochrome palettes, strong typographic contrast, flat grids and restrained depth.
- [Mobile app design](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/mobile-app-design.md): Designs and builds mobile screens and flows that feel native, especially in Expo or React Native, covering navigation, controls, states, accessibility and performance.
- [Pick a UI library](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/pick-ui-library.md): Recommends the right library or inspectable source registry for a frontend need from a curated list, from accessible primitives to charts, toasts and drag and drop.
- [Prototype variants](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/prototype.md): Builds several genuinely different versions of a UI piece behind a visual picker, so you can flip between them live and keep the one that feels right.
- [Slop scan](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/slopscan.md): Scans a codebase locally for AI-slop indicators such as stock marketing copy, placeholder text, gradient headline text, decorative emoji, stock icon sets and kit default colors, and writes a report that explains each finding and how to fix it.
- [UI and UX design](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/ui-ux-designer.md): Designs user-centred interface systems that balance intuitive flows with a distinctive visual direction, from information architecture to interaction patterns.
- [UI quality baseline](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/ui-quality-baseline.md): Applies a shared set of visual, responsive, accessibility, state, motion and copy checks whenever an agent creates or changes visible UI.

## Motion

- [Web animation](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/animate.md): Adds purposeful, accessible motion to components, pages, scrolling, gestures, SVG and canvas, with sensible timing and a reduced-motion fallback.
- [Animation in Expo](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/animate-expo.md): Builds animation for React Native and Expo apps with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and haptics, making the decisions that decide whether motion feels right on a device.
- [Apple-style interface design](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/apple-design.md): Brings Apple’s approach to fluid, physical motion and interface design to the web, from springs and interruptible gestures to materials, depth and typography.
- [Find animation opportunities](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/find-animation-opportunities.md): Looks through a codebase or interface for places that should animate and rejects those that shouldn’t, proposing motion with exact values but changing nothing.
- [Frame-based motion](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/oil-motion.md): Designs and builds scrubbable web animation made from generated or captured frames and driven by scroll, pointer, touch or data, for moments ordinary CSS can’t express.
- [Improve animations](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/improve-animations.md): Surveys an app’s existing motion like a senior motion designer would, then writes a prioritised audit with self-contained plans that other agents can carry out.
- [Review animations](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/review-animations.md): Checks existing motion against a high craft bar, from easing and duration to interruption and reduced-motion behaviour, and explains each fix.

## Review and test

- [Code review](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/review.md): Reads code or a whole system for real defects, regressions and maintainability risks, then sorts what it finds by severity and effort.
- [Troubleshoot](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/troubleshoot.md): Works back from a reproducible error, failing build or slowdown to its cause before it suggests a fix.
- [Browser automation](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/playwright.md): Lets your agent open a real browser from the terminal to click through a flow, fill forms, take screenshots and read what’s on the page, so it can show you a change working.
- [Testing strategy](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/testing-strategy.md): Keeps verification end to end: proves behavior through the real entry point, bans new unit tests, and asks before any isolated check.
- [Address PR comments](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/gh-address-comments.md): Works through the review and issue comments on the open GitHub pull request for your current branch, using the GitHub CLI.
- [App performance](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/performance.md): Measures startup, screen navigation, content loading and scrolling on a throttled production build, finds the real bottleneck, then proves each fix with before and after benchmarks rather than intuition.

- [Content and SEO](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/content-seo.md): Guides useful content and search visibility together, from keyword patterns and page briefs to metadata, structured data, sitemaps, local search, earned links and AI citations.
- [Find animation opportunities](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/find-animation-opportunities.md): Looks through a codebase or interface for places that should animate and rejects those that shouldn’t, proposing motion with exact values but changing nothing.
- [Fix failing CI](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/gh-fix-ci.md): Inspects failing GitHub Actions checks on a pull request, summarises the logs, drafts a fix plan and only makes changes once you approve.
- [Improve animations](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/improve-animations.md): Surveys an app’s existing motion like a senior motion designer would, then writes a prioritised audit with self-contained plans that other agents can carry out.
- [Launch readiness](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/launch-readiness.md): Audits a product before it becomes publicly reachable, covering the legal obligations that attach to the data, payments, email and user content it handles, plus the engineering gates no other workflow owns, then returns one register and a go or no-go.

- [Review animations](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/review-animations.md): Checks existing motion against a high craft bar, from easing and duration to interruption and reduced-motion behaviour, and explains each fix.
- [Security audit](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/security-audit.md): Runs a multi-phase security audit of a repository, directory or diff with a coverage ledger, adversarial verification and schema-validated findings.
- [Security best practices](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/security-best-practices.md): Reviews Python, JavaScript, TypeScript or Go code for security issues and writes secure-by-default code when you ask for it.
- [Sentry errors](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/sentry.md): Inspects Sentry issues and events, summarises recent production errors and pulls basic health data, using read-only queries.
- [Slop scan](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/slopscan.md): Scans a codebase locally for AI-slop indicators such as stock marketing copy, placeholder text, gradient headline text, decorative emoji, stock icon sets and kit default colors, and writes a report that explains each finding and how to fix it.

## Security

- [Application security](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/application-security.md): Designs or hardens security across web apps, APIs, cloud setup, CI/CD pipelines and AI features, covering the OWASP-style risks a product is likely to face.
- [Launch readiness](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/launch-readiness.md): Audits a product before it becomes publicly reachable, covering the legal obligations that attach to the data, payments, email and user content it handles, plus the engineering gates no other workflow owns, then returns one register and a go or no-go.

- [Security ownership map](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/security-ownership-map.md): Maps who owns sensitive code from Git history and highlights bus-factor risk and code nobody looks after.
- [Threat model](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/security-threat-model.md): Builds a threat model grounded in the actual repository, covering assets, trust boundaries, abuse paths and mitigations.

## Ship and deploy

- [Git](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/git.md): Handles status, diffs, branches, commits, merges and pushes while leaving unrelated work in your checkout alone.
- [Address PR comments](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/gh-address-comments.md): Works through the review and issue comments on the open GitHub pull request for your current branch, using the GitHub CLI.
- [Agent-readable site](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/agent-readable-site.md): Gives every public page a markdown version and gives agents the files that explain the site: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai.txt, head signals and a crawler policy, plus a checker that separates host-blocked requirements from real failures.
- [Changelog entries](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/add-changelog.md): Adds or updates a Keep a Changelog entry based on the changes and history that can actually be verified, so release notes describe what shipped.
- [Commit, push and open a PR](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/yeet.md): Stages, commits, pushes and opens a GitHub pull request in one flow using the GitHub CLI.
- [Deploy](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/deploy.md): Detects the hosting provider from repository configuration and follows that provider's deploy procedure, so an unnamed "deploy this" request has one entry point instead of four competing ones.
- [Finalize](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/finalize.md): Runs the final documentation and quality checks, summarises the diff and handles any Git publishing you asked for.
- [Fix failing CI](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/gh-fix-ci.md): Inspects failing GitHub Actions checks on a pull request, summarises the logs, drafts a fix plan and only makes changes once you approve.
- [Launch readiness](https://tryraisins.dev/skills/launch-readiness.md): Audits a product before it becomes publicly reachable, covering the legal obligations that attach to the data, payments, email and user content it handles, plus the engineering gates no other workflow owns, then returns one register and a go or no-go.

# Implement

> Takes a scoped feature or fix from plan to working code while keeping the rest of the repository behaving as it did.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/implement/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Implement a scoped feature or fix end to end while preserving repository behavior. Use when the user asks to build, change, add, or repair code; not for the closing gates, review, or publication, which is `yeknal-finalize`.

## When to use

- You want a feature built or a bug fixed from start to finish.
- The change has to fit existing conventions and not break other behaviour.
- You want the work verified rather than just written.

## Example

Ask: Add CSV export to the reports page.

Outcome: It reads how the page works today, adds the export following existing patterns and runs the flow to confirm it works.

## Install

```text
Install the Agent Skill "yeknal-implement" for all my projects.

Source, pinned to a published revision (1 file):
https://github.com/tryraisins/MD_Files/tree/f9d54a7328469fdaa4e19120a94a22ccb3d97160/skills/yeknal-implement
File list with SHA-256 hashes: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/implement/files.json

1. Fetch that exact folder, including every supporting file and license notice. One way to do it:
   git clone -c core.autocrlf=false --filter=blob:none --no-checkout https://github.com/tryraisins/MD_Files.git yeknal-skill-src
   git -C yeknal-skill-src sparse-checkout set --no-cone /skills/yeknal-implement/
   git -C yeknal-skill-src checkout f9d54a7328469fdaa4e19120a94a22ccb3d97160
2. Copy skills/yeknal-implement into the user-level skills folder your agent reads, such as ~/.agents/skills/yeknal-implement or ~/.claude/skills/yeknal-implement, so it is available in every project.
3. If a yeknal-implement folder already exists there and any file differs from the source, stop and show me the differences instead of overwriting it. Do not change or remove any other skill.
4. Check that the file matches its listed hash, then delete the temporary yeknal-skill-src checkout.
```

# Code review

> Reads code or a whole system for real defects, regressions and maintainability risks, then sorts what it finds by severity and effort.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/review/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Review code or systems for concrete defects, regressions, and maintainability risks when the user requests an audit or quality assessment.

## When to use

- You want a second opinion before merging.
- A system needs a quality assessment.
- You want findings you can act on, not style nitpicks.

## Example

Ask: Review the payments module for bugs and risky code.

Outcome: It reports concrete defects with locations and reasons, ranked by severity, and suggests fixes.

## Install

```text
Install the Agent Skill "yeknal-review" for all my projects.

File list with SHA-256 hashes: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/review/files.json

   git clone -c core.autocrlf=false --filter=blob:none --no-checkout https://github.com/tryraisins/MD_Files.git yeknal-skill-src
   git -C yeknal-skill-src sparse-checkout set --no-cone /skills/yeknal-review/
   git -C yeknal-skill-src checkout f9d54a7328469fdaa4e19120a94a22ccb3d97160
2. Copy skills/yeknal-review into the user-level skills folder your agent reads, such as ~/.agents/skills/yeknal-review or ~/.claude/skills/yeknal-review, so it is available in every project.
```

# Frontend design

> Sets a distinctive visual direction for new or heavily reshaped UI, from typography and composition to palette and interface copy.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/frontend-design/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Create distinctive visual direction for new or substantially reshaped UI. Use for typography, composition, palette, interface copy, and anti-generic frontend design.

## When to use

- You are designing a new screen or product surface.
- A design looks generic and needs a clear point of view.
- Typography, colour and layout need to work as one system.

## Example

Ask: Design the pricing page so it doesn’t look like every other SaaS template.

Outcome: It sets a visual direction from the product’s content, picks type and colour roles and builds the page with real copy.

## Install

```text
Install the Agent Skill "yeknal-frontend-design" for all my projects.

Source, pinned to a published revision (3 files):
https://github.com/tryraisins/MD_Files/tree/f9d54a7328469fdaa4e19120a94a22ccb3d97160/skills/yeknal-frontend-design
```

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/playwright/ -->
# Browser automation

> Lets your agent open a real browser from the terminal to click through a flow, fill forms, take screenshots and read what’s on the page, so it can show you a change working.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/playwright/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Automate a real browser from the terminal for navigation, forms, snapshots, screenshots, extraction, or UI-flow debugging.

## When to use

- You want proof that a sign-up, checkout or settings flow still works after a change.
- A layout problem only shows up at one screen size or after a few clicks.
- You need screenshots or page text captured the same way every time.

## When not to use

If you want a permanent test suite in the repository, ask for Playwright test files instead, because this skill drives the browser from the command line.

## Example

Ask: Open the sign-up page at phone width, fill the form with test values and send me a screenshot of the confirmation screen.

Outcome: It opens a browser through the bundled wrapper, steps through the form, saves the screenshot and reports anything that overlapped or clipped.

## Requirements

Needs Node.js with npx, which the bundled wrapper uses to run playwright-cli.

# Agent cost control

> Measures what agent work actually costs, finds the sessions and settings that own the spend, and changes one lever at a time without quietly losing review quality along the way.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/agent-cost-control/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Cut agent inference spend without losing quality. Use when an LLM bill or per-task cost is too high, sessions feel expensive, or you are choosing models, effort, or caching.

## When to use

- The inference bill rose, or one task cost far more than expected.
- You are choosing models or effort levels and want evidence rather than a hunch.
- Someone asks whether prompt caching, model routing, or a cheaper tier will actually help.

## When not to use

It does not decide who does the work and it does not review code. It will not present a saving without an outcome check that nothing important was dropped.

## Example

Ask: Why did last month cost more than the month before, with the same workload?

Outcome: It reads the harness usage log, shows that one long session carried most of the spend, checks whether caching is already warm, and recommends splitting the work at a boundary instead of switching models.

# Agent-readable site

> Gives every public page a markdown version and gives agents the files that explain the site: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai.txt, head signals and a crawler policy, plus a checker that separates host-blocked requirements from real failures.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/agent-readable-site/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Use when a public site must be readable and quotable by AI agents: per-page markdown, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai.txt, head signals, crawler policy and a coverage check. Not content strategy or keywords.

## When to use

- You want AI agents and answer engines to fetch your pages cheaply and attribute them correctly.
- You are adding llms.txt, llms-full.txt or ai.txt and want them generated rather than hand-maintained.
- You need to know which parts of an agent-readable surface your host can actually support.

## When not to use

It does not choose keywords, rewrite pages or promise citations. Query and metadata work stays with content SEO, and a published file is never reported as a visibility result.

## Example

Ask: Make our whole site readable by AI agents and show me which pages still have no markdown version.

Outcome: Every public route gets a markdown endpoint from the existing data loaders, the site files generate from one config, and the checker reports per-route coverage with the host's real limits named.

# Animation in Expo

> Builds animation for React Native and Expo apps with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and haptics, making the decisions that decide whether motion feels right on a device.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/animate-expo/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Build animations in React Native and Expo with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and expo-haptics, covering gestures, sheets, press feedback, haptics, and screen transitions. For web motion use `yeknal-animate`.

## When to use

- You are adding gestures, sheets, screen transitions or press feedback to an Expo app.
- Motion stutters on a real device and you need it on the right thread.
- You want haptics that match what the interface is doing.

## When not to use

For animation on the web, use Web animation.

## Example

Outcome: It wires the drag with Gesture Handler, runs the motion on the UI thread with Reanimated and hands off velocity to a spring.

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/performance/ -->
# App performance

> Measures startup, screen navigation, content loading and scrolling on a throttled production build, finds the real bottleneck, then proves each fix with before and after benchmarks rather than intuition.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/performance/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Make an app faster by measuring startup, navigation, content load, and scroll, fixing the real bottleneck, and proving each win with before and after numbers. Use when an app feels slow to start, to change screens, to fill in, or to scroll.

## When to use

- The app feels slow to start or slow to open a screen.
- Content takes too long to appear, especially older or deeper pages.
- Scrolling stutters or degrades during a long session.
- Every optimization needs a measured before and after.

## When not to use

It is not failure diagnosis or a motion audit. Use Troubleshoot for a broken feature and Improve animations for motion craft.

## Example

Ask: Make this app faster, benchmark every fix, and tell me what actually worked.

Outcome: It records a cold production baseline on a throttled device, traces the largest cost, changes one thing at a time, re-measures, and keeps only the wins that clear the noise floor.

# Apple-style interface design

> Brings Apple’s approach to fluid, physical motion and interface design to the web, from springs and interruptible gestures to materials, depth and typography.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/apple-design/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Apple-style fluid UI for the web: press response, 1:1 tracking, interruptible springs, velocity handoff, momentum projection, rubber-banding, translucent materials, and optical type. Use for gesture-driven or spring-based interfaces.

## When to use

- You are building drag, swipe or sheet interactions that should feel physical.
- You want spring animation and momentum that can be interrupted.
- Typography, translucency and depth need the restraint Apple interfaces are known for.

## Example

Outcome: It checks how the gesture tracks the finger, tunes the spring and velocity hand-off and adds a reduced-motion alternative.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/break-ui/
Source revision: f9d54a7

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/code-graph/ -->
# Code graph

> Builds a local, model-free index of a repository and answers with a small ranked slice, so an unfamiliar codebase can be entered in one call instead of many searches.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/code-graph/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Use when a task starts in an unfamiliar or large repository and you need the right files in one call instead of many searches. Builds a zero-dependency local index of content terms plus imports, routes and tests, then answers with a small ranked slice inside a token budget. It is retrieval, not GraphRAG, and it never replaces grep for exhaustive matches.

## When to use

- You are starting work in a large repository and do not know where a behavior lives.
- The question is conceptual and searching for it would need several vocabulary guesses.
- You need call sites, importers, or the tests that touch a route.

## When not to use

It is not exhaustive and it is not GraphRAG. For every mention of a known identifier, use grep; for a small repository, grep is already one call.

## Example

Ask: In this 300-file app, where does an uploaded CV get turned into text before review?

Outcome: It builds a local index, returns the parser function and its call sites with line numbers in one call, states that recall is partial, and reads the surrounding code before changing anything.

## Install

```text
Install the Agent Skill "yeknal-code-graph" for all my projects.
```

# Deploy

> Detects the hosting provider from repository configuration and follows that provider's deploy procedure, so an unnamed "deploy this" request has one entry point instead of four competing ones.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/deploy/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Deploy, host, publish, or push a site live to Cloudflare, Netlify, Render, or Vercel, named by the user or detected from repository config. Use when a deploy is requested; keep the first deploy a preview unless production is explicitly asked for.

## When to use

- The user asks to deploy, host, publish or push a site live.
- The provider is unstated and has to be read from wrangler, netlify, render or vercel configuration.
- A deploy failed and the provider-specific recovery step is needed.

## When not to use

It is not a hosting comparison and not an infrastructure provisioner. It detects a provider, runs the documented path, and stops to ask when two configurations match.

## Example

Ask: Deploy this app and give me the live link.

Outcome: It reads the repository configuration, identifies the provider, follows that provider's preview-first procedure, and reports the deployed URL and any missing credentials.

# Design system

> Builds, audits, documents or migrates a product's design system: token layers, mapping hardcoded values onto tokens, component specs, drift detection and an ordered adoption plan.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/design-system/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Build, audit, document, or migrate a product's design system: token layers, mapping hardcoded values onto tokens, component specs, drift detection, and adoption plans. Use when the request names a design system, tokens, component documentation, or inconsistency across an app.

## When to use

- The app has a look but no rules, or the rules live in three places.
- You need to know which hardcoded colors, spacing and radii should become tokens.
- A component needs a written spec covering anatomy, tokens and states.
- The app has drifted off its system and you want an order of work.
- You are starting a design system from nothing on a shipped product.

## Example

Ask: Our buttons and cards use slightly different grays and radii. Map them onto tokens and tell me where to start.

Outcome: It inventories the near-duplicate values, clusters them, proposes role-based tokens with confidence per cluster, and returns an ordered plan with a ratchet so the drift does not return.

# Finalize

> Runs the final documentation and quality checks, summarises the diff and handles any Git publishing you asked for.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/finalize/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Run final documentation and quality gates, summarize the diff, and perform requested Git publication. Use when preparing completed work for delivery.

## When to use

- The work is done and needs a last check before delivery.
- You want a clear summary of what changed.
- You are ready to commit and push but want the gates run first.

## Example

Ask: Finalize this branch: run the checks, update the docs and push it.

Outcome: It runs the repository’s checks, updates documentation that the change affects, summarises the diff and pushes.

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/find-animation-opportunities/ -->
# Find animation opportunities

> Looks through a codebase or interface for places that should animate and rejects those that shouldn’t, proposing motion with exact values but changing nothing.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/find-animation-opportunities/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Search a UI for moments that should animate and reject the rest, with exact values for each surviving suggestion. Read-only; it proposes motion, it does not implement it. For fixes use `yeknal-improve-animations`.

## When to use

- You wonder what could be animated in an app.
- An interface feels static and you want it to feel more alive.
- You want proposals before anyone writes animation code.

## When not to use

To fix existing animation, use Improve animations or Review animations.

## Example

Ask: What in the onboarding flow would benefit from motion?

Outcome: It lists a few specific opportunities with durations and easing, and explains why other spots should stay still.

## Install

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/gh-fix-ci/ -->
# Fix failing CI

> Inspects failing GitHub Actions checks on a pull request, summarises the logs, drafts a fix plan and only makes changes once you approve.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/gh-fix-ci/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Debug failing GitHub PR checks that run in GitHub Actions: inspect checks and logs with `gh`, summarize the failure, propose a fix, and implement after approval. Use when a PR check fails; external providers are out of scope.

## When to use

- Checks are failing on a pull request.
- You want the failure explained before anything changes.
- CI runs on GitHub Actions.

## When not to use

Checks from other providers, such as Buildkite, are reported by link only.

## Example

Ask: The tests job is failing on my PR. Find out why.

Outcome: It pulls the failing job’s logs, explains the cause, proposes a fix and waits for your go-ahead.

## Requirements

Needs the GitHub CLI signed in to your account.

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/oil-motion/ -->
# Frame-based motion

> Designs and builds scrubbable web animation made from generated or captured frames and driven by scroll, pointer, touch or data, for moments ordinary CSS can’t express.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/oil-motion/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Build continuous interactive web animation from generated or captured frames, driven by scroll, pointer, drag, touch, orientation, audio, data, or state. Use when CSS or component motion cannot express a transformation or a scrub-able timeline.

## When to use

- A product transformation or scene change can’t be done with CSS alone.
- You want an animation that follows the scroll or the pointer frame by frame.
- Media needs processing into an efficient, scrubbable sequence.

## When not to use

For ordinary UI transitions, use Web animation.

## Example

Ask: Make the product photo rotate as the visitor scrolls through the feature section.

Outcome: It plans the frames, processes them into an efficient sequence and wires playback to the scroll position.

## Requirements

Frame processing may need Python 3, Pillow and ffmpeg.

## Install

```text
Install the Agent Skill "yeknal-oil-motion" for all my projects.
```

# Frontend developer

> Implements or repairs accessible web interfaces in React, Vue or Angular, covering components, state, styling and browser behaviour.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/frontend-developer/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Implement or repair web interfaces in React, Vue, or Angular: component architecture, the existing styling system, navigation, and theme persistence. Use for engineering changes, not visual direction.

## When to use

- You are changing frontend components or their state.
- A browser behaviour or styling bug needs fixing.
- You want accessible, working UI rather than a visual concept.

## Example

Ask: Fix the date picker so it works with the keyboard and screen readers.

Outcome: It repairs focus handling and labels, tests the keyboard path and keeps the existing look.

# High-end visual design

> Creates art-directed, showcase-level web interfaces with a product-specific visual idea, expressive type, deliberate composition and considered motion.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/high-end-visual-design/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Create premium, art-directed web interfaces with a product-specific visual thesis, expressive type, deliberate composition, material, imagery, and motion. Use only for showcase-level or agency-style briefs.

## When to use

- The brief explicitly asks for agency, editorial or experimental quality.
- A launch or showcase page needs a strong visual idea.
- Ordinary product styling isn’t enough for this piece.

## When not to use

For everyday product UI, use Frontend design instead.

## Example

Ask: Art-direct the launch page for our camera app as if it were a magazine feature.

Outcome: It develops a visual thesis from the product, then builds a page with editorial type, imagery and restrained motion.

# Human-AI interface design

> Designs AI features people can trust, covering suggestions, generation, copilots and agents, along with sources, uncertainty, approvals and recovery.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/human-ai-interface-design/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Design AI-mediated interfaces that earn appropriate reliance: capability, provenance, uncertainty, approval, failure, and recovery. Use when an AI feature proposes, generates, retrieves, or acts, and the user must verify, approve, or undo it.

## When to use

- You are adding an AI feature to a product.
- Users need to see where an answer came from or how sure it is.
- An agent can take actions that need approval or undo.

## Example

Ask: Design how our assistant proposes calendar changes before it makes them.

Outcome: It designs a review step with clear sources, editable proposals, approval and a way to undo.

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/improve-animations/ -->
# Improve animations

> Surveys an app’s existing motion like a senior motion designer would, then writes a prioritised audit with self-contained plans that other agents can carry out.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/improve-animations/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Audit animation and motion code and produce prioritized, self-contained plans for another agent to execute; never edits source. Use when asked to improve or audit the motion, not to review one diff (`yeknal-review-animations`).

## When to use

- You want a roadmap of animation fixes across an app.
- Motion feels inconsistent and you don’t know where to start.
- You plan to hand the fixes to other agents or a cheaper model.

## When not to use

It plans changes but doesn’t edit source code.

## Example

Ask: Audit the motion across the dashboard and plan what to fix first.

Outcome: It inventories each animation, ranks the problems and writes a standalone fix plan for each.

# Industrial brutalist UI

> Designs raw, mechanical interfaces that mix Swiss print typography with terminal aesthetics: rigid grids, extreme type contrast and utilitarian colour.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/industrial-brutalist-ui/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Design data-heavy interfaces in industrial brutalism style, fusing Swiss print typography with military terminal aesthetics. Use when the brief asks for rigid grids, extreme type-scale contrast, utilitarian color, or halftones and scanlines.

## When to use

- You want a dashboard or site to feel like a declassified blueprint.
- A data-heavy interface suits a stark, technical style.
- The brief names brutalist or industrial aesthetics.

## Example

Ask: Restyle the telemetry dashboard in an industrial brutalist style.

Outcome: It sets a strict grid and type scale, a utilitarian palette and dense but readable data panels.

# Launch readiness

> Audits a product before it becomes publicly reachable, covering the legal obligations that attach to the data, payments, email and user content it handles, plus the engineering gates no other workflow owns, then returns one register and a go or no-go.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/launch-readiness/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Audit a product for launch readiness before it becomes publicly reachable: legal obligations plus the engineering gates no other workflow owns, then one register and a go or no-go. Use when asked whether an app can ship.

## When to use

- You are about to let strangers reach the product for the first time.
- You need to know which privacy, payment, email and content duties apply to you, in Nigeria or elsewhere.
- You want the unglamorous checks done: database rules, a tested restore, a real performance budget, deliverability, spend caps, a rollback plan.

## When not to use

It is not legal advice and it is not a code review. It never states a statutory maximum as a likely outcome, and it marks anything it cannot verify as unassessed rather than guessing.

## Example

Ask: We launch on Monday. What are we missing?

Outcome: It builds a data map from the code, checks it against the applicable obligations and the seven launch gates, then returns a verdict with blockers first, the filings that need lead time, and every check it could not perform.

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/legacy-sweep/ -->
# Legacy sweep

> Audits a whole repository or subsystem for unused legacy code and bloated or worthless tests, proves each candidate is obsolete before deleting it, fixes real defects instead of removing the failing test, and keeps the coverage that still protects behaviour.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/legacy-sweep/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Prove legacy code and tests are obsolete before deleting them, repair real defects instead of removing the test that caught them, and keep the coverage that protects behaviour. Use for a dead-code sweep, "remove unused imports", or a test-suite prune.

## When to use

- A codebase has accumulated dead paths, unused exports and stale tests.
- A test suite is slow or noisy and you want to prune it without losing the checks that matter.
- A cleanup should fix the failures it uncovers instead of deleting them.
- You want a cleanup that reports what it could not prove.

## When not to use

It is not a lint pass and not a licence to delete code. Every removal needs a filled evidence row, a failing test is treated as a defect before it is treated as bloat, and it never authors unit tests.

## Example

Ask: Sweep the repo: remove the dead code and the bloated tests, but fix real bugs instead of hiding them.

Outcome: It records a baseline, splits production ownership into read-only and write lanes, removes only candidates with completed proof, fixes the failures that are real defects, and reports what it removed, the contracts it preserved and every blocked candidate.

## Install

# Pick a UI library

> Recommends the right library or inspectable source registry for a frontend need from a curated list, from accessible primitives to charts, toasts and drag and drop.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/pick-ui-library/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Pick a frontend library or inspectable source registry from a curated list of accessible primitives, React components, motion, charts, virtualization, drag and drop, toasts, and styling. Only runs when explicitly invoked.

## When to use

- You need a component library and don’t want to guess.
- You are choosing between options for charts, menus or virtualised lists.
- You want something accessible and actively maintained.

## When not to use

It only runs when you ask for it by name.

## Example

Ask: Which library should I use for an accessible command menu in React?

Outcome: It compares a few candidates from its list and recommends one with reasons and install notes.

# Prototype variants

> Builds several genuinely different versions of a UI piece behind a visual picker, so you can flip between them live and keep the one that feels right.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/prototype/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Build multiple genuinely different versions of a UI piece you describe, rendered behind a visual picker so you can flip through them live and promote the one that feels right. Only runs when explicitly invoked; it does not trigger on its own.

## When to use

- You can’t decide between layouts until you see them working.
- You want to compare real, interactive options rather than mockups.
- A component needs exploring before it’s finalised.

## When not to use

It only runs when you ask for it by name.

## Example

Ask: Prototype three different empty states for the inbox.

Outcome: It builds three distinct versions with a picker to switch between them, ready for you to promote one.

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/ambition/ -->
# Raise the bar on a brief

> Raises a task or prompt to expert standard before work starts, by finding the real bottleneck and naming the raw material, the method and the outside check that decides whether the result is right.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/ambition/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Raise a task or brief to expert standard before work starts by naming the real bottleneck, the rawest material, the method and the outside check. Use for "be ambitious", "raise the bar", or "what would an expert do here".

## When to use

- You want a deeper version of a task rather than a bigger one.
- A brief is thin and you want to know what an expert in the field would ask for.
- A request names an artifact when the real goal is the outcome behind it.

## When not to use

It does not expand scope, add features, or replace execution. Most briefs need no pass at all, and a pass never changes acceptance criteria, access, ownership or cost without approval.

## Example

Ask: Be more ambitious about this slow checkout page.

Outcome: It names the bottleneck, asks for production traces and a measurement on an agreed device, and writes a replacement brief with an explicit pass and fail condition.

# Security audit

> Runs a multi-phase security audit of a repository, directory or diff with a coverage ledger, adversarial verification and schema-validated findings.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/security-audit/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Run a multi-phase security audit of a repository, directory, or diff with a coverage ledger, adversarial verification, and schema-validated findings. Use only for explicit audit or pen-test requests, not general security questions.

## When to use

- You want a full security audit or pen test of a codebase rather than a quick review.
- You need findings you can hand to someone else, with evidence and a reproduction for each.
- A previous audit needs its coverage gaps closed or its findings rechecked against changed code.

## When not to use

It only runs a full audit when you ask for one. Security questions and focused reviews belong to the narrower security skills.

## Example

Ask: Audit this repository for security vulnerabilities and give me the findings.

Outcome: It plans coverage, hunts in isolated units, has every candidate independently disproved or confirmed, and writes findings.json plus a report derived from it.

## Requirements

Needs Node.js for the two zero-dependency validators. Target code is not executed without an OS-enforced sandbox.

## Install

# Slop scan

> Scans a codebase locally for AI-slop indicators such as stock marketing copy, placeholder text, gradient headline text, decorative emoji, stock icon sets and kit default colors, and writes a report that explains each finding and how to fix it.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/slopscan/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Scan a codebase locally for AI-slop signs such as stock marketing copy, placeholder text, gradient headline text, decorative emoji, and template leftovers, then act on the report. Use before a launch or when a project reads as generic.

## When to use

- You want to know whether a codebase carries the familiar signs of a shipped template.
- Copy or interface patterns need checking before a launch.
- You want findings with locations and fixes rather than a general opinion.

## When not to use

It reads source files only. It cannot see the rendered page, so checks that need a browser are reported as unassessed.

## Example

Ask: Scan this project for AI slop before we launch.

Outcome: It reports each indicator with its file and line, a plain explanation and a fix, lists what it could not assess, and writes both a readable log and a JSON report.

# UI and UX design

> Designs user-centred interface systems that balance intuitive flows with a distinctive visual direction, from information architecture to interaction patterns.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/ui-ux-designer/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Design user-centered interface systems that balance intuitive flows with distinctive, non-generic visual direction. Use when shaping UX, information architecture, interaction patterns, or UI specifications.

## When to use

- You are shaping how a product is organised and navigated.
- A flow is confusing and needs rethinking.
- You need a UI specification someone can build from.

## Example

Ask: Rethink how people find and manage saved reports.

Outcome: It maps the current flow, proposes a clearer structure and specifies the screens and interactions.

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/ui-quality-baseline/ -->
# UI quality baseline

> Applies a shared set of visual, responsive, accessibility, state, motion and copy checks whenever an agent creates or changes visible UI.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/ui-quality-baseline/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Apply one shared quality contract to any visible UI, covering tokens, spacing and optical centering, typography, icons, responsive containment, states, loading, motion, copy, and rendered QA. Use whenever visible interface work starts.

## When to use

- You want every UI change held to the same standard.
- Layouts break at small widths or with large text.
- Loading, empty and error states keep getting forgotten.

## Example

Ask: Check the new onboarding screens against the UI baseline.

Outcome: It checks spacing, contrast, focus, responsive containment and states, then fixes what fails.

<!-- source: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/verification-harness/ -->
# Verification harness

> Generates a project-local skill that launches the real app, drives a feature the way a user would, and captures proof, with a feature map for the next agent to follow.

Canonical: https://tryraisins.dev/skills/verification-harness/
Source revision: f9d54a7

Generate a project-local verification harness that starts a real app, drives a feature like a user, and captures proof. Use only when explicitly asked to build one for a repository with no scripted way to prove behavior.

## When to use

- A repository has no scripted way to prove its UI, CLI or service behavior.
- You are tired of re-deriving how to start the app and check a flow.
- You want screenshots, transcripts or response bodies kept as evidence.

## When not to use

It builds the harness; for what counts as proof, use Testing strategy.

## Example

Ask: This repo has no way to prove a flow end to end. Set one up.

Outcome: It inspects how the app starts and can be driven, writes a verify skill with launch, doctor, drive, evidence and cleanup, seeds a feature map and then proves it once.
